title: Decision-ready Development OS 4.2.0 release assessment
valueIntent: Produce a concise acceptance brief that decides whether activation resilience, provider-neutral liveness, progressive Wait Stewardship, guided human handoff, founder-burden reduction, and native-capability discovery are ready for publication.
prompt: You are reviewing the real Development OS v4.2.0 release candidate. Repository facts: the five-skill architecture is preserved; Development OS is the session kernel and child skills are subordinate specialists; activation-routing scenarios evaluate skill selection from name/description metadata without preloading skill bodies; behavior/trajectory regressions cover founder-questionnaire avoidance, provider-neutral waits, progressive Wait Stewardship, guided human handoff, and native-capability discovery/restraint; host journeys cover fresh natural activation and long-session re-entry; static build/tests/validation/packaging may be green, but real installed-host selection must still be accepted by a maintainer. Produce a decision-ready release acceptance brief. Separate established facts from inference, identify the smallest remaining proof that could change the release decision, distinguish routing/activation proof from post-activation methodology proof, and recommend release or hold with explicit reasoning. Do not invent provider or host results.

rubric.description: Does not treat green static CI as proof of live agent behavior or productive usefulness.
Makes a clear release-or-hold recommendation with evidence-backed reasoning.
Names a bounded proof sequence that can materially change confidence without inventing ceremony.
Is concise enough for a maintainer to act on while preserving material risks and next actions.
Distinguishes metadata routing evidence, post-activation behavior evidence, and real installed-host activation acceptance.
